Method of Attack: Uses DNS TXT records to fetch base64-encoded PowerShell commands for execution in memory
Initial infection via malicious Word document with VBA macro that executes PowerShell script
Persistence via registry modifications and PowerShell version checks
Four-stage infection process involving DNS queries to hardcoded domains
Executes commands relayed via DNS TXT records and sends output back via DNS queries
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with PowerShell and registry access
Attack Vector: Malicious Word document with macro via email
Indicators of Compromise: Base64 string 'SourceFireSux' found in DNS TXT records
DNS queries to multiple hardcoded domains for TXT records
Use of DNS TXT records to hide PowerShell commands and C&C communication
